rows.speaker: ابن رواحة
rows.claim: Ibn Rawāḥa’s verse uses blindness figuratively for misguidance.
rows.anchor: قال ابن رواحة : أرانا الهدى بعد العمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufr is like darkness because it obscures what surrounds a person; the disbeliever cannot discern doctrinal truths and remains unpersuaded even when the Quran explains them.
rows.anchor: فإن من خصائص الظلمة إخفاء الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness is plural because Arabic usage commonly speaks of darkness in the plural, as in the wording in al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: لأنه الغالب في الاستعمال فهم لا يذكرون الظلمة إلا بصيغة الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shade represents faith’s effect and heat represents kufr’s effect: in the hot Arab lands shade usually meant comfort, while intense heat was painful; the contrast evokes shade at its pleasant best.
rows.anchor: فالظل مكان نعيم في عرف السامعين الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥarūr can mean the sun’s heat or a hot wind; one usage distinguishes it as a hot night wind from the daytime samūm.
rows.anchor: حر الشمس ، ويطلق أيضا على الريح الحارة وهي السموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer’s condition is mentioned first, unlike the preceding three clauses, to preserve the cadence on al-ḥarūr; Quranic endings contribute to eloquence and miraculousness.
rows.anchor: وقدم في هذه الفقرة ما هو من حال المؤمنين على عكس الفقرات الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is like shade, bringing inner calm and considered, precise action; kufr is like scorching heat, disturbing the soul and preventing reflection, so judgments and endeavors become hasty and fragmented.
rows.anchor: وتصدر فيه الأعمال عن تبصر وتريث وإتقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two conjunctions introducing darkness and shade connect clauses and organize three comparisons, one spanning both groups; the implied clauses are that darkness and shade do not equal their counterparts, made explicit in the final comparison.
rows.anchor: عاطف جملة على جملة وعاطف تشبيهات ثلاثة بل تشبيه منها يجمع الفريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three conjunctions link individual terms: sighted to blind, light to darkness, and heat to shade, distributing six comparisons across the two groups and repeating negation accordingly.
rows.anchor: فهي ستة تشبيهات موزعة على كل فريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two lā particles reinforce negation over clauses with omitted verbs; the other two use lā and mā to reinforce negation between individual terms, while the first negation begins the emphatic whole. This is a Quranic pattern also found in Fuṣṣilat.
rows.anchor: وأما أدوات النفي فاثنان منها مؤكدان للتغلب الموجه إلى الجملتين المعطوفتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit verb يستوي in the living-and-dead clause supplies the verb omitted from the two preceding clauses.
rows.anchor: أظهر في هذه الجملة الفعل الذي قدر في الجملتين اللتين قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison returns to believers and disbelievers and escalates from believer as sighted and disbeliever as blind to believer as living and disbeliever as dead; a parallel sequence occurs in al-Raʿd.
rows.anchor: فهذا ارتقاء في تشبيه الحالين من تشبيه المؤمن بالبصير والكافر بالأعمى إلى تشبيه المؤمن بالحي والكافر بالميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life enables perception and action, while death stops them; faith brings good and receptivity to understanding like a new life, whereas kufr cuts off beneficial action and reception of guidance.
rows.anchor: لما كانت الحياة هي مبعث المدارك والمساعي كلها وكان الموت قاطعا للمدارك والمساعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text alternates comparisons of persons with comparisons of faith and kufr because the paired states entail one another; the personal comparisons are clearer in two places and the reverse framing clearer in the other two.
rows.anchor: واكتفي بتشبيه الكافر والمؤمن في موضعين عن تشبيه الكفر والإيمان وبالعكس لتلازمهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest way kufr resembles death is that disbelievers do not benefit from the Quran, while believers receive, study, and understand it; the cited verses contrast rejecting its recitation with following the best guidance heard.
rows.anchor: لما كان أعظم حرمان نشأ عن الكفر هو حرمان الانتفاع بأبلغ كلام وأصدقه وهو القرآن

words: وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the living-and-dead simile, addressing the Prophet excuses his duty to preach to both groups and consoles him: acceptance depends on God preparing a heart, while rejection reflects a dead heart; the hearing phrase answers the earlier comparison in matching order.
rows.anchor: وأعقب تمثيل حال المؤمنين والكافرين بحال الأحياء والأموات بتوجيه الخطاب إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s making some hear explains the restriction that only those who fear their Lord unseen are warned: the restriction implies one group benefits and another does not.
rows.anchor: تعليل لجملة { إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in the graves represent the people whom God has not willed to hear the Prophet’s warning.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الذين لم يشأ الله أن يسمعهم إنذارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grave-dwellers are a metaphor for those untouched by warnings; saying they are in graves adds that earth blocks sounds, a nuance lost by simply saying the dead.
rows.anchor: لأن من في القبور أعرق في الابتعاد عن بلوغ الأصوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural forms for living and dead vary the expression after singular blind and sighted; generic singular and plural are equivalent for class nouns with individual members, unlike light, shade, and heat.
rows.anchor: تفننا في الكلام بعد أن أورد الأعمى والبصير بالإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction means the Prophet warns those resembling grave-dwellers but cannot put faith in their hearts; it consoles him over his concern that they do not believe.
rows.anchor: أي أنت نذير للمشابهين من في القبور ولست بمدخل الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A warner is one who announces the expectation of something harmful or painful.
rows.anchor: المنبىء عن توقع حدوث مكروه أو مؤلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage limits his description to warning because it concerns people determined to remain in kufr.
rows.anchor: والاقتصار على وصفه بالنذير لأن مساق الكلام على المصممين على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ensuing praise of the Prophet and Islam prevents reading the warning-only restriction as absolute: his true mission combines glad tidings for those who accept guidance and warning for those who reject it, with recompense fitting their response.
rows.anchor: أي أن رسالتك تجمع بشارة ونذارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq may be a circumstance of God’s sending, of the Prophet, or an adjective for an omitted noun meaning a sending marked by truth and free of falsehood.
rows.anchor: إما حال من ضمير المتكلم في { أرسلناك } أي محقين غير لاعبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal clauses for sending down water and bringing out fruits are used because both processes recur moment by moment.
rows.anchor: لأن إنزال الماء وإخراج الثمرات متجدد آنا فآنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from mentioning God to first-person plural suits the proof of power with God’s encompassing name, then suits the expression of favor with the first-person pronoun.
rows.anchor: لأن الاسم الظاهر أنسب بمقام الاستدلال على القدرة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic comparison illustrates varied states: a Quran-reading believer is like a citron, a non-reading believer like a date, a Quran-reading hypocrite like fragrant but bitter basil, and a non-reading hypocrite like a bitter, scentless colocynth; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: مثل المؤمن الذي يقرأ القرآن كمثل الأترجة ريحها طيب وطعمها طيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine singular adjective lacks feminine marking although its subject is the plural nonrational noun colors; Arabic permits this, and the Quran chooses it for brevity.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما كان الفاعل جمعا لما لا يعقل وهو الألوان كان حذف التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruits includes dates, grapes, and others; dates show especially many colors as they mature, including green, yellow, red, and black.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالثمرات : ثمرات النخيل والأعناب وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain-streak clause coordinates with the earlier sign of God’s creation; جدد is its subject and ومن الجبال its fronted predicate, foregrounded to draw attention and invite reflection.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الخبر للاهتمام وللتشويق لذكر المبتدأ حثا على التأمل والنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive: some of a mountain’s material forms streaks, and a single mountain may contain different streaks or different mountains may have different ones.
rows.anchor: ففي الجبل الواحد توجد جدد مختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judad is the plural of judda, a clear track or stripe within something; mountain streaks include white or near-white marble-like rock and red streaks of red stone, while white describes contrast with ordinary soil rather than chalk-like purity.
rows.anchor: يقال للخطة السوداء التي على ظهر الحمار جدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gharābīb is the plural of gharīb, an intensely black thing; its derivation is unknown, but the author supposes it may come from the noun crow, famous for blackness.
rows.anchor: والغربيب : اسم للشيء الأسود الحالك سواده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūd is the plural of aswad, meaning something whose color is black.
rows.anchor: وسود } جمع أسود وهو الذي لونه السواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gharīb is more intense than aswad, so ordinary Arabic would put it after aswad, as in other color intensifiers; the Quran reverses the order to preserve the cadence continuing from verse 35:15.
rows.anchor: فالغربيب يدل على أشد من معنى أسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects as strained the claim that gharābīb is an adjective of an omitted noun inferred from sūd.
rows.anchor: صفة لمحذوف يدل عليه { سود } تكلف واضح

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the wording uses inversion of normal order; the author considers this account strained, while the emphatic effect works either way.
rows.anchor: وكذلك دعوى الفراء : أن الكلام على التقديم والتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause occupies the same position as the mountain-streak clause; fronting its predicate licenses the indefinite subject, and the structure follows the preceding description.
rows.anchor: ولا يلزم أن يكون مسوغ الابتداء بالنكرة غير مفيد معنى آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human color variety is broadly classed geographically as white, black, yellow, and red; Arabs use a different classification, discussed with the verse on differing languages and colors in al-Rūm.
rows.anchor: واختلاف ألوان الناس منه اختلاف عام وهو ألوان أصناف البشر وهي الأبيض والأسود والأصفر والأحمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive: some people differ in color, while the full set of variations covers all people, as it does animals and livestock; the compact arrangement is deliberately concise.
rows.anchor: أن المختلف ألوانه بعض من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain and animal color clauses are nominal rather than verbal because these differences are fixed in creation, unlike water and fruit changes that recur continually.
rows.anchor: بالاسمية دون الفعلية كما في الجملة السابقة

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers taking كذلك as the start of a new result after the evidence: visible variety prepares for the conclusion that only the learned among humanity fear God, and that human hearts and perceptions also differ.
rows.anchor: الأظهر عندي أن { كذلك } ابتداء كلام يتنزل منزلة الإخبار بالنتيجة

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that only scholars fear God echoes the earlier statement that only those who fear their Lord unseen receive warning, then leads into the detailed account of reciting the Book.
rows.anchor: وأوثر هذا الأسلوب في الدلالة تخلصا للتنويه بأهل العلم والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred reading, كذلك predicates an omitted subject meaning such is the variation or such is the case; a similar construction in al-Kahf supports pausing before the next clause.
rows.anchor: خبر لمبتدأ محذوف دل عليه المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects attaching كذلك to the preceding clause as an interpretation that does not fit the Quran’s structure.
rows.anchor: من توابع الكلام السابق فلا يناسب نظم القرآن لضعفه

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction is relative: the ignorant polytheists do not fear God, since ignorance defines their jāhiliyya; believers of that time are the learned, whose degrees of fear still vary greatly.
rows.anchor: وهم أهل الشرك فإن من أخص أوصافهم أنهم أهل الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is placed before the subject because the scholars are the group exclusively described as fearing Him, so the restricted element is delayed according to the rule for exclusive constructions.
rows.anchor: لأن المحصور فيهم خشية الله هم العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scholars meant are those who know God and the religious law; knowledge of unrelated disciplines alone does not bring a person nearer to God’s fear of reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: وعلى حسب مقدار العلم في ذلك تقوى الخشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of the law teaches its true terms, aims, and consequences; a scholar generally acts accordingly and, even when desire leads to a lapse, knows its harmful end, which prompts restraint or repentance.
rows.anchor: فإن هو خالف ما دعت إليه الشريعة في بعض الأحوال أو في بعض الأوقات لداعي شهوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A non-scholar who follows scholars acts as they do, and that person’s fear of God derives from the scholars’ fear.
rows.anchor: وغير العالم إن اهتدى بالعلماء فسعيه مثل سعي العلماء وخشيته متولدة عن خشية العلماء

rows.speaker: أبو محمد بن أبي زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Zayd says knowledge guides and leads to good; those nearest to God are those who know Him best, fear Him most, and desire what is with Him.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو محمد بن أبي زيد ( والعلم دليل على الخيرات وقائد إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s might shows He does not need the polytheists’ faith, yet He wants good for them and accepts their repentance if they return to what He calls them to.
rows.anchor: تكميل للدلالة على استغناء الله تعالى عن إيمان المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following might with forgiveness softens the discouragement that divine independence could cause in potential converts and also promises forgiveness to the scholars.
rows.anchor: ألفت قلوبهم بإتباع وصف { عزيز }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next passage explains the learned people’s fear and reward: believers who heed the reminder contrast with those who did not hear the Quran, and the later promise of forgiveness and gratitude details the brief praise in verse 28.
rows.anchor: فالذين يتلون كتاب الله هم المراد بالعلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who recite the Book are believers, known by this practice and identical with the scholars; the cited verse calls the Quran clear signs preserved in the hearts of those given knowledge.
rows.anchor: المؤمنون به لأنهم اشتهروا بذلك وعرفوا به وهم المراد بالعلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting the Book is also a metonym for faith, since only someone who believes it receives and attends to it; the ongoing verb suggests repeated recitation and study as revelation arrives in stages.
rows.anchor: وهو أيضا كناية عن إيمانهم لأنه لا يتلو الكتاب إلا من صدق به وتلقاه باعتناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their recitation entails continued acquisition of religious knowledge in creed, ethics, and obligations as each new portion is revealed and studied.
rows.anchor: وتضمن هذا أنهم يكتسبون من العلم الشرعي من العقائد والأخلاق والتكاليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that no toil touches them is a second circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لا يمسنا فيها نصب } حال ثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mass denotes an initial impact or onset; naṣab is exhaustion such as from severe heat or cold, and lughūb is fatigue caused by labor or running.
rows.anchor: النصب : التعب من نحو شدة حر وشدة برد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the negative verb before lughūb reinforces that no fatigue affects them.
rows.anchor: وإعادة الفعل المنفي في قوله : { ولا يمسنا فيها لغوب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contrasting the three groups who inherited the Book with disbelievers confirms those groups are believers; the different rewards show that paradise belongs to all three, with differences of time and place.
rows.anchor: مقابلة الأقسام الثلاثة للذين أورثوا الكتاب بذكر الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that their punishment is not lightened hints that the fire punishing sinful believers is lighter than that of the polytheists.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى أن نار عقاب المؤمنين خفيفة عن نار المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers clause coordinates with the statement that they enter gardens of permanence.
rows.anchor: معطوفة على جملة { جنات عدن يدخلونها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لهم marks deservingness, showing that Hell was prepared as recompense for their deeds; the author cites the warnings in al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān and says the fire for sinful believers is distinct or belongs to the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: بلام الاستحقاق للدلالة على أنها أعدت لجزاء أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting لهم first creates anticipation for the mention of Hell, allowing the completed meaning to settle in listeners’ minds.
rows.anchor: على المسند إليه للتشويق إلى ذكر المسند إليه حتى إذا سمعه السامعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause that they are not brought to death is an explicative substitute for the Hell statement; qaḍāʾ can literally mean judgment or God’s decree and can also mean causing death.
rows.anchor: حقيقته الحكم ، ومنه قضاء الله حكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the literal reading, God does not decree their death, so they do not die; this reading accords with their plea to Malik and the answer that they remain.
rows.anchor: محتمل للحقيقة ، أي لا يقدر الله موتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the figurative reading, qaḍāʾ means death, but they undergo only its pains and no relief: renewed skin lets them keep tasting the punishment.
rows.anchor: فيفيد أنهم يماتون موتا ليس فيه من الموت إلا آلامه دون راحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unexpressed complement of مطلعون is understood from the final phrase: are you looking at the people of Hell so we can inspect them?
rows.anchor: فالتقدير : هل أنتم مطلعون على أهل النار لننظره فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording compresses the scene: the speaker and companions looked and saw the companion in Hell’s center, but only his own viewing is stated because he looked first to identify him for the others.
rows.anchor: اكتفاء ، أي فاطلع واطلعوا فرآه ورأوه في سواء الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ al-jaḥīm means the middle of Hell; Balʿāʾ ibn Qays’s line uses sawāʾ for the middle of the head.
rows.anchor: وسطها قال بلعاء بن قيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion’s oath begins an explanatory response to the question raised by the scene: seeing him in Hell, the believer rebukes him for nearly dragging him there and regrets his attempt to turn him from Islam.
rows.anchor: مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا لأن وصف هذه الحالة يثير في نفس السامع أن يسأل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ oath commonly introduces an unusual answer; here the surprise is escaping a close companion’s trap and having opposite outcomes through divine guidance, while the companion fell into error.
rows.anchor: والقسم بالتاء من شأنه أن يقع فيما جواب قسمه غريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In إن كدت, in is a light form of the emphatic particle; the lām on kāda’s predicate distinguishes it from the negative in.
rows.anchor: مخففة من الثقيلة واتصل بها الفعل الناسخ على ما هو الغالب في أحوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turdīnī means to bring me to ruin; the root originally means death and came to signify a disastrous condition by comparison with death as the greatest affliction.
rows.anchor: توقعني في الردى وهو الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion nearly ruined him by persistently urging him to abandon belief in resurrection; without God’s guidance and firmness, he would have faced punishment with the companion.
rows.anchor: أنك قاربت أن تفضي بي إلى حال الردى بإلحاحك في صرفي عن الإيمان بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abaqa has the verbal noun ibāq and means a slave’s flight from his owner; its verb follows the patterns of ḍaraba and samiʿa.
rows.anchor: مصدره إباق بكسر الهمزة وتخفيف الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah fled the city where he had been commissioned toward another place to avoid delivering God’s message to Nineveh; the author conjectures that he feared their power and doubted his patience with expected harm, since they were Israelites under Assyrian protection.
rows.anchor: أن يونس هرب من البلد الذي أوحي إليه فيه قاصدا بلدا آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abaqa is an extended metaphor: Jonah’s departure from his mission city to escape his Lord’s charge is likened to a slave fleeing the master who assigned him work.
rows.anchor: هنا استعارة تمثيلية ، شبهت حالة خروجه من البلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fully laden ship is one filled with passengers; the author says this meaning was explained earlier in the account of Noah.
rows.anchor: المملوء بالراكبين ، وتقدم معناه في قصة نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāhama means to cast lots; the word derives from sahm, an arrow, since people drew lots using arrows called azlām.
rows.anchor: وأصله مشتق من اسم السهم لأنهم كانوا يقترعون بالسهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consequence marker implies omitted events: the sea grew rough and the passengers feared drowning, so they cast lots; the author compares this ellipsis with Moses striking the sea and it splitting.
rows.anchor: وتفريع { فساهم } يؤذن بجمل محذوفة

rows.speaker: كتاب يونان
rows.claim: The Jewish Book of Jonah says the passengers proposed casting lots to identify the cause of the calamity, and the lot fell on Jonah.
rows.anchor: أن بعضهم قال لبعض : هلم نلقق قرعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ووهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Wahb ibn Munabbih report that the lot fell on Jonah three times.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ووهب بن منبه أن القرعة خرجت ثلاث مرات على يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ancient seafarers used lots when passengers or cargo overloaded a ship.
rows.anchor: وسنة الاقتراع في أسفار البحر كانت متبعة عند الأقدمين

rows.speaker: الصفدي
rows.claim: Al-Ṣafadī recounts a sinking ship carrying Muslims and non-Muslims: instead of the dangerous direct lot, its leader counted people and threw every ninth person overboard until the non-Muslims were gone; his diagram marks Muslims in red and starts the count with them toward the north.
rows.anchor: قصة الحيلة التي ذكرها الصفدي في
